summary: Lane County, OR lookout site: camp 1919, L-5 cab 1933, staffed to 1941, gone by 1968; four concrete footings remain per Oregon Hikers.

facts.design: L-5 cab on a 10x10 ground house (1933)
facts.status_note: Lookout removed by 1968 per FFLOS and Forest Lookouts (Oregon Hikers says last lookout decommissioned in the 1970s); four concrete footings remain at the summit per Oregon Hikers

access.note: Former lookout site reached by hiking in the Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness, per Oregon Hikers field guide; road access not described

visit.trail_note: Oregon Hikers lists a 7.3 mi hike with 2,075 ft gain to the former lookout site

events.note: Lookout camp started (FFLOS: starting with a camp in 1919)
L-5 cab built; Forest Lookouts describes a 10x10 L-5 lookout ground house built in 1933
Gordon Stanley sent to spend the summer as look-out fireman for the Forest Service (Eugene Guard item)
Lookout staffed 85 days; last dated staffing record found
Oregon Hikers: the last lookout on the summit was erected in 1958. Not confirmed by the register or Forest Lookouts.
FFLOS: gone by 1968. Forest Lookouts: lookout removed 1968. firelookout.com: R.I.P. 1933-1968.
Registered May 7, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says Willamette National Forest; Oregon Hikers says Umpqua National Forest. Not resolved here; the story reports both. The Lane County location in the brief is not affected.

Register and Forest Lookouts give removal by 1968; Oregon Hikers describes a last lookout erected in 1958 and decommissioned in the 1970s. Recorded removal as 1968 (two sources); the 1958 and 1970s dates are kept in notes as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Oregon Hikers is a volunteer field guide (contributor bobcat), not an official record. Its 1958 build and 1970s decommission conflict with the register and Forest Lookouts (gone by 1968); the 1958 structure may be a later cabin, which we could not confirm. Forest disagreement (Willamette vs Umpqua) unresolved. Brief elevation 1719.7 m (5642 ft) and design L-5 match the register; no correction. No official source describes the summit today. Trail data is from the hiking listing only and was not checked on the ground; the story does not give directions.
